kept.note: Enthusiastic yes: "¿Vamos? —¡De una!". Informal, very common among young people.

example.es: —¿Pedimos pizza? —¡De una, me muero de hambre!
example.en: —Shall we order pizza? —Totally, I'm starving!

kept.note: Strong denial: no way, not even close. Also "ni ahí con eso": not into it. Informal.

example.es: Ni ahí voy a esa fiesta, no conozco a nadie.
example.en: No way am I going to that party, I don't know anyone.

kept.note: Shrugging filler when unsure or vague. Often at the end: "...y qué sé yo". Neutral, everyone says it.

example.es: No sé, podemos ir al cine, al parque, qué sé yo.
example.en: I don't know, we could go to the movies, the park, whatever.

kept.note: Filler like English "like": "tipo, no sé". Also means around with times: "tipo ocho", around eight.

example.es: Nos vemos tipo nueve en la puerta del bar.
example.en: See you around nine at the bar door.

kept.note: The go-to "of course" in Argentina: "¡Obvio!" or "obvio que sí". Informal but used by everyone.

example.es: —¿Venís al asado? —¡Obvio! ¿Qué llevo?
example.en: —Are you coming to the barbecue? —Of course! What should I bring?

kept.note: Full on, all the way: "estoy a full con el laburo". Anglicism, very common and informal.

example.es: Esta semana estoy a full con los exámenes.
example.en: This week I'm totally swamped with exams.

kept.note: "¡Cualquiera!" or "qué cualquiera": that's ridiculous, makes no sense. Also "hacer cualquiera": act crazy.

example.es: ¿Te cobraron diez lucas por un café? ¡Cualquiera!
example.en: They charged you ten grand for a coffee? That's nuts!

kept.note: Filler to wrap up or change topic when there is nothing more to say. Very typical porteño rhythm.

example.es: Bueno, nada, eso te quería contar. Hablamos después.
example.en: Well, anyway, that's what I wanted to tell you. Talk later.

kept.note: "¿Todo bien?" is a standard greeting; "todo bien" also means no problem or it's fine.

example.es: Hola, che, ¿todo bien? Hace mil que no te veo.
example.en: Hey, all good? I haven't seen you in ages.

kept.note: That has nothing to do with it, or "not at all" as a reply. "Es re nada que ver": it's totally off.

example.es: ¿Que yo estoy enojado? Nada que ver, estoy cansado.
example.en: Me, angry? Not at all, I'm tired.

kept.note: Reaction to news, real or feigned surprise: "¡Mirá vos!". Can sound ironic with a flat tone.

example.es: —Se casa Martín. —¡Mirá vos! No sabía que tenía novia.
example.en: —Martín is getting married. —Well, look at that! I didn't know he had a girlfriend.

kept.note: Total agreement: "¡Tal cual!", that's exactly it. Informal and very frequent.

example.es: —Este país es una montaña rusa. —Tal cual.
example.en: —This country is a roller coaster. —Exactly.

kept.note: Casual greeting, or "¿qué onda con...?" to ask what's going on with something. Informal.

example.es: ¿Qué onda, che? ¿Salimos esta noche?
example.en: What's up? Are we going out tonight?

kept.note: Excellent, a ten out of ten: "quedó de diez". Casual and positive.

example.es: La comida estuvo de diez, gracias por invitarnos.
example.en: The food was perfect, thanks for inviting us.

kept.note: "Es fija": it's certain, it'll happen for sure. From horse-racing slang. Informal.

example.es: Si llueve, es fija que el subte se llena.
example.en: If it rains, it's a sure thing the subway fills up.

kept.note: Placed before a noun for emphasis: "alto quilombo", "alta fiesta". Young, very informal.

example.es: Anoche fue alta fiesta en lo de Juli.
example.en: Last night was a huge party at Juli's.

kept.note: A lot: "te quiero una banda", "había una banda de gente". Informal, very common.

example.es: Había una banda de gente en la cancha.
example.en: There were a ton of people at the stadium.

kept.note: A little, briefly: "esperá un toque", "un toque de sal". Softens requests. Informal.

example.es: Esperame un toque que termino y salimos.
example.en: Wait a sec, I'll finish and we'll head out.

kept.note: Closes a deal or topic: "listo, nos vemos mañana". Also "¿listo?" to check agreement. Everyday word.

example.es: Listo, entonces paso a buscarte a las siete.
example.en: Okay, so I'll pick you up at seven.

kept.note: "¡Olvidate!" means absolutely, count on it, not forget it. Context decides; tone is enthusiastic.

example.es: —¿Me ayudás con la mudanza? —¡Olvidate! Ahí estoy.
example.en: —Will you help me move? —You bet! I'll be there.

kept.note: Enthusiastic agreement among young people: "—¿Vamos? —¡De más!". Informal.

example.es: —¿Te copa ir a la costa? —¡De más!
example.en: —Up for going to the coast? —Totally!

kept.note: Without fail, one way or another: "tenés que venir sí o sí". Neutral, everyone uses it.

example.es: El viernes tenemos que terminar esto sí o sí.
example.en: We have to finish this by Friday no matter what.

kept.note: "No da" means it's not appropriate or not worth it: "no da ir así vestido". Informal.

example.es: No da llegar tarde a la entrevista, salgamos ya.
example.en: It's not cool to be late to the interview, let's leave.

kept.note: Before a noun for emphasis: "cero ganas", "cero onda". Informal, very common.

example.es: Hoy tengo cero ganas de cocinar, pidamos algo.
example.en: I have zero desire to cook today, let's order something.

kept.note: Whatever, it's done, let it go. Also to decide on impulse: "ya fue, me lo compro".

example.es: Ya fue, no me contestó. Me voy a dormir.
example.en: Forget it, he didn't answer. I'm going to bed.

kept.note: Short for tranquilo: "todo tranca", everything's calm. Also "tranca" as reassurance: relax. Informal.

example.es: Tranca, no pasa nada, lo arreglamos mañana.
example.en: Chill, it's no big deal, we'll fix it tomorrow.

kept.note: "¡Sonaste!" warns someone they're in trouble. From "sonar", to be doomed. Jokey or serious.

example.es: Si tu vieja ve esa nota, sonaste.
example.en: If your mom sees that grade, you're toast.

kept.note: Describes a friendly, easygoing person or vibe: "es re buena onda". Opposite: "mala onda".

example.es: El profe nuevo es re buena onda.
example.en: The new teacher is really nice.

kept.note: "Estar quemado": mentally fried from work or study. "Tengo la cabeza quemada". Informal.

example.es: Después de seis horas de reunión estoy re quemado.
example.en: After six hours of meetings I'm totally fried.

kept.note: A slump, sadness or letdown: "¡qué bajón!". "Estar de bajón": to feel down. Very common.

example.es: Qué bajón que se suspendió el recital.
example.en: What a downer that the concert got cancelled.

kept.note: To be crazy or overwhelmed: "estás de la cabeza". Also stressed out. Informal.

example.es: Con tres laburos, Pablo está de la cabeza.
example.en: With three jobs, Pablo has lost it.

kept.note: "Estar podrido de algo": sick and tired of it. Informal; literally rotten.

example.es: Estoy podrido de que me cancelen a último momento.
example.en: I'm sick of people cancelling at the last minute.

kept.note: Delighted, tickled pink: "está chocha con el nieto". Warm, a bit old-fashioned but common.

example.es: Mi abuela está chocha con el perrito nuevo.
example.en: My grandma is thrilled with the new puppy.

kept.note: To get angry: "no te calientes". "Estar caliente" can mean angry, but careful: it also means horny.

example.es: No te calentés, fue sin querer.
example.en: Don't get mad, it was an accident.

kept.note: To get bored stiff. Informal, very common; "me embolé" after a dull movie.

example.es: Me embolé en la clase y me fui a la mitad.
example.en: I got bored in class and left halfway through.

kept.note: Distracted, or into other things now: "ya está en otra". Informal.

example.es: Te hablo y no me escuchás, estás en otra.
example.en: I'm talking to you and you're not listening, you're miles away.

kept.note: To get tangled up overthinking something: "no te enrosques". Informal.

example.es: No te enrosques, seguro no te contestó porque estaba laburando.
example.en: Don't overthink it, he surely didn't reply because he was working.

kept.note: "Estar rayado": obsessed with something, or a bit crazy. Informal, youthful.

example.es: Está rayado con el gimnasio, va todos los días.
example.en: He's obsessed with the gym, he goes every day.

kept.note: Beside oneself with rage, or wild: "estaba re sacado". Informal.

example.es: El vecino vino re sacado por el ruido.
example.en: The neighbor came over furious about the noise.

kept.note: Excited and carried away: "estoy embalado con el proyecto". Informal.

example.es: Está embalado con la banda, ensaya todos los días.
example.en: He's psyched about the band, he rehearses every day.

kept.note: "Estar a mil": extremely busy or wound up. Informal.

example.es: Perdón que no te llamé, estoy a mil con la mudanza.
example.en: Sorry I didn't call, I'm swamped with the move.

kept.note: "Estar al horno": to be in a real fix. Literally in the oven. Informal.

example.es: Mañana rindo y no estudié nada, estoy al horno.
example.en: I have the exam tomorrow and didn't study, I'm screwed.

kept.note: Like a frozen computer: stuck, blank. "Me quedé tildado": my mind went blank. Informal.

example.es: Me preguntó el nombre y me quedé tildado.
example.en: He asked my name and I just froze.

kept.note: Distracted or forgetful: "soy re colgado". "Me colgué": I forgot. Informal.

example.es: Perdón, me colgué y no te devolví el llamado.
example.en: Sorry, I spaced out and didn't call you back.

kept.note: Grumpy, crabby: "hoy el jefe está cruzado". Informal.

example.es: Hoy mi viejo anda cruzado, mejor no le hables.
example.en: My dad is in a bad mood today, better not talk to him.

kept.note: Bitter, no fun: "no seas amargo". Used for someone who won't join in. Informal.

example.es: Dale, no seas amargo y vení a bailar.
example.en: Come on, don't be a party pooper and come dance.

kept.note: An intense crush or obsession: "tiene un metejón con la vecina". Lunfardo, still used.

example.es: Tiene un metejón con esa chica que no se le pasa.
example.en: He has a crush on that girl he just can't shake.

kept.note: "Estar tragado": totally smitten with someone. Informal.

example.es: Está re tragado con su compañera de facultad.
example.en: He's head over heels for his classmate.

kept.note: Utterly exhausted: "llegué fusilado". Informal; literally shot by firing squad.

example.es: Después del turno doble llegué fusilado a casa.
example.en: After the double shift I got home wiped out.

kept.note: "Estar del tomate": to be nuts. Jokey, informal.

example.es: Querés cruzar la cordillera en bici, estás del tomate.
example.en: You want to cross the Andes by bike, you're nuts.

kept.note: To be unable to stop laughing, often at the wrong moment: "me tenté". Very Argentine.

example.es: En el velorio me tenté y tuve que salir.
example.en: At the wake I got the giggles and had to step out.

kept.note: A scare: "me pegué un julepe bárbaro". Rioplatense, a bit old-fashioned.

example.es: Me pegué un julepe cuando sonó el teléfono a las tres.
example.en: I got a real fright when the phone rang at three.

kept.note: Anger or frustration: "me da bronca", it makes me mad. Very common everyday word.

example.es: Me da bronca que nadie avise cuando llega tarde.
example.en: It makes me mad that nobody warns when they're late.

kept.note: Argentines say agarrar, never coger, for take or grab: "agarrá el colectivo", "agarrá por Corrientes".

example.es: Agarrá la segunda a la derecha y ya llegaste.
example.en: Take the second right and you're there.

kept.note: "Rajar" is to fire or kick out: "lo rajaron". "Rajá de acá": get out of here. Informal.

example.es: Lo rajaron del laburo por llegar siempre tarde.
example.en: He got fired for always showing up late.

kept.note: To sneak a look: "pispeá qué hay en la heladera". Informal, playful.

example.es: Pispeé el regalo antes del cumple.
example.en: I peeked at the present before the birthday.

kept.note: To grab or swipe with a quick hand movement, or snatch at something. Informal.

example.es: Me manoteó el celular de la mano en el bondi.
example.en: He snatched the phone out of my hand on the bus.

kept.note: To scrape by or escape something: "zafé del examen". "Zafa": it's passable. Very common.

example.es: No estudié mucho, pero zafé con un cuatro.
example.en: I didn't study much, but I scraped by with a pass.

kept.note: Everyday verb for check or verify, preferred over "comprobar". Neutral.

example.es: Chequeá que la puerta quede cerrada antes de salir.
example.en: Check that the door is locked before you leave.

kept.note: To click with someone, often romantically: "pegamos onda enseguida". Informal.

example.es: Pegamos onda en la fiesta y ahora salimos.
example.en: We hit it off at the party and now we're dating.

kept.note: "Me clavó": stood me up. "Clavar el visto": leave on read. Also stick someone with a cost.

example.es: Me clavó una hora en el bar y nunca vino.
example.en: He left me waiting an hour at the bar and never came.

kept.note: To get into something: "me enganché con la serie". Also to join in. Informal.

example.es: Me enganché con la serie y la terminé en dos días.
example.en: I got hooked on the show and finished it in two days.

kept.note: To burn through cash: "me patiné el sueldo". Informal.

example.es: Me patiné todo el aguinaldo en una semana.
example.en: I blew my whole bonus in a week.

kept.note: To go bankrupt or run out of money: "se fundió el negocio". Also to be worn out. Informal.

example.es: Se le fundió el negocio con la crisis.
example.en: His business went bust with the crisis.

kept.note: To screw things up: "la embarré". Informal, not rude.

example.es: La embarré, le conté la sorpresa a Juan.
example.en: I messed up, I told Juan about the surprise.

kept.note: Besides hurry, in Argentina it means to corner or press someone for answers: "lo apuré y confesó".

example.es: Lo apuré un poco y terminó contando todo.
example.en: I pressed him a bit and he ended up telling everything.

kept.note: To think up a plan or idea: "estoy craneando algo". Informal.

example.es: Estamos craneando una sorpresa para su cumple.
example.en: We're cooking up a surprise for her birthday.

kept.note: "Mandarse una macana": to blunder. "Mandarse" also means to go boldly or do on impulse. Informal.

example.es: Me mandé una macana con el auto de mi viejo.
example.en: I screwed up with my dad's car.

kept.note: The everyday Argentine word for scold, instead of regañar: "me retó la maestra".

example.es: Mi vieja me retó por llegar tarde.
example.en: My mom told me off for coming home late.

kept.note: To leave, often in a hurry: "me las tomo". "¡Tomátelas!": get lost. Informal.

example.es: Bueno, me las tomo que mañana madrugo.
example.en: Well, I'm off, I have to get up early tomorrow.

kept.note: To calm down or get your act together: "rescatate". Youth slang, very common.

example.es: Rescatate un poco, ya te pasaste con el vino.
example.en: Get a grip, you've had way too much wine.

kept.note: To stop doing something annoying: "¡cortala!". Informal, common with kids and friends.

example.es: Cortala con el celular y ayudame a poner la mesa.
example.en: Put down the phone and help me set the table.

kept.note: Start or head off: "¿arrancamos?", "arranqué el gimnasio". Much more common than empezar in speech.

example.es: ¿Arrancamos? Ya son las diez.
example.en: Shall we get going? It's already ten.

kept.note: To eye someone up or keep an eye on them: "te está fichando". Informal.

example.es: Ese flaco te está fichando desde que llegamos.
example.en: That guy has been checking you out since we arrived.

kept.note: To be unfaithful: "lo gorrearon". From "poner los cuernos". Informal.

example.es: Se separaron porque ella lo gorreaba con un compañero.
example.en: They split up because she was cheating on him with a coworker.

kept.note: To hit the target or guess correctly: "la embocaste". Informal.

example.es: Con el regalo la embocaste, le encantó.
example.en: You nailed it with the present, she loved it.

kept.note: Slang sense: to make fun of or show someone up: "me descansó". Youthful, informal.

example.es: Me descansaron todo el día por el corte de pelo.
example.en: They teased me all day about my haircut.

kept.note: To fail someone on an exam: "me bocharon en química". Student slang.

example.es: Me bocharon en el final de matemática.
example.en: They flunked me on the math final.

kept.note: To prepare and serve mate in rounds: "¿quién ceba?". Also to egg someone on.

example.es: ¿Cebás vos? A mí siempre me sale lavado.
example.en: Will you pour the mate? Mine always comes out weak.
